title: Voyager 2 visited all four giant planets on one mission
body: Voyager 2 flew past Jupiter in 1979, Saturn in 1981, Uranus in 1986 and Neptune in 1989. A rare alignment let NASA use each planet's gravity to help steer the spacecraft towards the next.
takeaway: A route through space can use gravity to change direction and speed without making every change with fuel.
source: NASA Science, Voyager 2 and Planetary Voyage
visual: a small spacecraft passing the edge of a giant planet with other planets faint in the distance

title: Chandrayaan-1 helped find signs of water on the Moon
body: India launched Chandrayaan-1 in 2008 carrying NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper. The instrument measured reflected light, revealing patterns linked to water and hydroxyl on the lunar surface.
takeaway: A sensor in orbit can detect chemical signatures in sunlight without collecting a physical sample.
source: NASA Science, Chandrayaan-1 and Moon Impact Probe
visual: a small orbiter passing over a rough strip of the Moon's surface

title: Part of Pluto's bright heart is a plain of nitrogen ice
body: New Horizons imaged Pluto's heart-shaped region in 2015. Its western lobe, known as Sputnik Planitia, is a broad basin largely covered in frozen nitrogen.
takeaway: The substance that makes up most of Earth's air can form a landscape on a far colder world.
source: NASA Science, Frozen: Ice on Earth and Well Beyond
visual: a broad pale ice plain with polygonal patches surrounded by dark hills on Pluto
